source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Standard repositioning techniques being considered just as safe for a client with a suspected spinal injury","B":"Log rolling generally lacking any established safety rationale despite being a routine part of spinal injury care","C":"It maintains spinal alignment during repositioning, reducing the risk of further spinal cord injury from twisting or bending motions","D":"This particular technique being needed only during the first 24 hours after the injury, rather than throughout recovery"}}
source_row.rationale: Log rolling technique maintains spinal alignment during repositioning, reducing the risk of further spinal cord injury from twisting or bending motions, an important safety practice for clients with suspected or confirmed spinal injury throughout their care, not only the initial period after injury.
source_row.source_detail: Purpose of Log Rolling for Spinal Injury Safety
source_row.source_name: AANN — Spinal Precaution and Log Rolling Guidelines
